scope: Actual CPython 3.11 publication and query execution using separate Spark 3.5 and Spark 4 environments. Private local commerce source authority; this does not qualify Truss, Unity Catalog, a production warehouse, formal verification, an OpenTelemetry receiver, process-kill durability, or a fresh virtual-environment build.
result: The original c7 public UMF receipt and dataset produced 11 objects, 10 edges, zero tombstones and 21 history rows. Independent checks cover the pinned table UUIDs and complete raw cell bags. Indexed String, count and first-hop queries returned the original expected bags, with 13 native integrity guards reporting zero violations, two actual schemas and four closed ordinary-role ACK intervals. Source, model and SQL were preserved.
failure: The earlier command D query failed while opening the WAL-mode journal read-only with CPython 3.9 / SQLite 3.54.0; no query report was released. Its log and copy-only diagnosis are retained. The original journal was not repaired. Command E succeeded with CPython 3.11 / SQLite 3.53.1 without repeating publication.
custody: All archived reports and artifacts match their original bytes. All 77 opening publication files are unchanged. The closing inventory has 79 files: a new zero-byte operations.sqlite-wal (SHA256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855) and a new 32768-byte operations.sqlite-shm (SHA256 fd4c9fda9cd3f9ae7c962b0ddf37232294d55580e1aa165aa06129b8549389eb). The full file set is therefore not identical. The coordination-file additions were observed; their exact byte-level cause was not captured. Root verified stopped Spark processes and the bounded PostgreSQL fixture; selected resource hashes were rechecked.
native_limits: This qualifies the original single-edge product-to-supplier fixture. Parallel-edge behavior, the distinct-neighbor correction, two-hop queries and general truncation behavior require separate execution evidence.
